dedupe_keys.name: characterizing the role of power grids in internet resilience grid failure zones and the netwattzap analysis tool 2023

description: This 2023 arXiv paper characterises how far the Internet depends on power grids by overlaying global power and Internet infrastructure. It finds that nearly 65% of public Internet infrastructure components sit in fewer than ten power grid failure zones, and that grid dependencies sharply limit the number of disjoint cloud availability zones: once the grids serving data centre locations are counted, the number of isolated AWS Availability Zones falls from 87 to 19. The paper also evaluates high-impact scenarios (extreme weather, solar superstorms, electromagnetic pulse and cyber attacks), and builds NetWattZap, an Internet resilience analysis tool that gives power-grid-dependency-aware deployment suggestions for infrastructure and application components under user requirements. Producer: Sangeetha Abdu Jyothi. Coverage: global. Access: the paper on arXiv; the abstract page and HTML version were read, and no code or data release was confirmed there. Licence and cost: free to read under the arXiv licence. Caveats: results rest on public infrastructure datasets with location uncertainty, and NetWattZap availability was not verified. Simulation uses: the failure-zone mapping supports cascading-failure and resilience models that couple power and digital networks. Related records: PeeringDB (data-peeringdb) and the ISOC Pulse IXP power substation dependency simulation (case_study-isoc-pulse-ixp-power-substation-dependency-simulation).
